{
  "reframes": [
    {
      "bottleneck": "Evaluation is serialized per feature: fit an SAE or choose a vector, then run up to 300-step closed-loop rollouts. One unbatched rollout idles the GPU during simulation and observation, and after roughly 150 rollouts x 135 features more spending mostly estimates rigid-task success more precisely.",
      "assumption": "The right unit of evidence is one whole episode for one steered feature, and nothing is known about contact control until that full episode succeeds or fails.",
      "reframe": "Change the unit of work to a short paired contact-window intervention: steer on/off for 10-30 steps around a canonical event such as grasp onset, plate-at-rack mouth, or towel-corner pull, and measure the change in contact state rather than task success. Use these windows as a screen; only directions that move contact variables earn long closed-loop rollouts.",
      "question": "For the top 50 existing SAE/conceptor directions and 50 matched random controls, what fraction produces |delta| > 2 noise SD in at least one measured contact variable within 20 steps, where the measured variables are wrist force/torque, object slip speed, insertion clearance, and cloth strain energy from marker motion, and what AUC does that contact delta have for held-out 300-step success?",
      "measure": "Reuse already-fit features. Build one instrumented real microtask, plate into rack plus towel corner over a peg, and one matching GPU sim. Run 100 paired on/off windows x 100 directions in sim, 20 steps each, about 40k policy steps and under one A100-day with batching; then run 20 paired real windows for the 20 most promising directions, 400 short trials, about 1-2 robot-days. Rough cost: under $1k GPU plus 2 robot-days and no new SAE sweep.",
      "compute_after": "Thousands of directions, layers, objects and contact states can be screened in parallel short windows. Extra compute buys coverage of contact regimes, then concentrates expensive closed-loop rollouts on the few directions with measured causal contact effects.",
      "exact": "Estimand: paired on/off change in contact variables during steps 5-25. Call a direction positive only if the effect has the same sign in at least 60% of windows, the paired bootstrap CI excludes 2 SD of actuator/sensor noise, and the contact-delta score predicts held-out 300-step success with AUC >= 0.8; treat AUC <= 0.6 as not worth pursuing.",
      "expected": "Most directions should be inert. A small set may change slip or insertion clearance for rigid contact; cloth effects are likely weaker or confounded with pose/visual state. If predictive, this should cut full rollouts by roughly 10-50x.",
      "fails_if": "Contact-window deltas have AUC < 0.6 for held-out success, real and sim disagree in sign on the same rigid microtask, or the effect appears only when camera and object pose are held fixed.",
      "closest_prior": "Largest cited sweep: 420,000+ rollouts and 520+ SAEs across six VLAs, arXiv:2603.19233; SAE cost derived from arXiv:2603.19183; parallel rollout nearest attempt: RLinf-VLA with 256 ManiSkill environments, arXiv:2510.06710v2."
    },
    {
      "bottleneck": "The objective is average or binary success on unperturbed rigid tasks. Once a feature helps pick-and-place, additional episodes buy the same point estimate and do not resolve the failures that matter for laundry and dish racks: slip, high force, entanglement, mis-seating and recovery.",
      "assumption": "A direction that raises mean success is useful for reliable household manipulation, and disturbances are either rare or will be handled by the same policy that succeeds in the nominal case.",
      "reframe": "Change the objective to a paired rare-tail and recovery claim: measure conditional failure and recovery under standard disturbances such as object offset, friction drop, cloth wrinkle and rack misalignment. Use batched perturbed episodes and rare-event splitting to resolve tails, and accept a direction only if it lowers failure probability without raising the high-force tail.",
      "question": "Under a fixed perturbation set of 1 cm/5 deg object offset, 30% friction drop, one folded cloth corner, and 5 mm rack misalignment, does any candidate direction reduce measured P(failure | perturbation) by at least 5 percentage points and reduce recovery steps by at least 25%, while not increasing the 95th-percentile contact force by more than 10 N?",
      "measure": "Cheapest gate: 2 candidate directions x 2 perturbations x 100 paired short sim episodes, 400 episodes total, under one A100-day with batched environments; then 20 paired real short trials per direction-perturbation on plate insertion and towel-corner pull, 160 real trials total, about 2 robot-days, with wrist force/torque and AprilTag/marker logging. Rough cost: under $1k GPU plus 2-3 robot-days.",
      "compute_after": "More compute buys tail resolution: parallel perturbed episodes across objects, disturbance magnitudes, VLA checkpoints and steering strengths. It changes the answer from helps-on-average to changes-the-failure-distribution.",
      "exact": "Report delta P_fail = P_fail(on) - P_fail(off) per perturbation with paired bootstrap CI. Pass only if the upper CI is below -0.05, the median recovery-step ratio is <= 0.75, and delta F95 <= +10 N. Fail fast if after 20 real paired trials the CI half-width on delta P_fail still exceeds 0.10.",
      "expected": "Rigid target-selection features likely move grasp choice but not slip or high-force tails. The general features whose ablation cut success from 39/40 to 0/40 may affect recovery, but for cloth the benefit may vanish outside the recorded pose or visual state.",
      "fails_if": "No direction clears delta P_fail <= -0.05 without a force-tail increase, or perturbation failures are dominated by perception/state-estimation error rather than steerable motor/contact features.",
      "closest_prior": "COAST conceptors raising pi0.5 on LIBERO-10 from 0.43 to 0.80 and about +40% on three real tasks; pi0.5 SAE steering on DROID and top-4 ablation 39/40 to 0/40; Goodfire robotics steering claims with no published numbers."
    },
    {
      "bottleneck": "The sweep holds the task coordinate frame and evaluation distribution nearly fixed. Grant-style absolute-coordinate motor programs mean more rollouts at the recorded spot can keep buying successes while saying nothing about laundry or dish racks in new poses.",
      "assumption": "An internal steering vector represents a portable skill, so moving the object, base or camera should preserve the intervention and pose randomization is an unnecessary extra cost.",
      "reframe": "Measure steering as a function of SE(3) displacement and re-express the intervention in an object-relative frame before scaling. Reorder the work as: estimate pose, transform the steering vector or hook, run randomized-pose microtrials, and only then launch a large sweep.",
      "question": "For a known effective pi0.5/DROID direction, what is the measured retention curve R(d, theta) = (success_on - success_off at displacement)/(success_on - success_off at recorded pose) over d in {0,5,10,20} cm and theta in {0,15,30,45} deg, and does object-relative transformation keep R(20 cm,45 deg) >= 0.8 while the untransformed vector falls below 0.5?",
      "measure": "Use no new SAE: reuse one known positive direction and one ablation-critical direction. On one real insertion or grasp task, run 25 paired trials at the recorded pose plus a 4x4 pose grid with 10 paired trials per cell, with and without the relative transform: 25 + 16 x 10 x 2 = 345 short trials, about 3-5 robot-days with AprilTag pose and force/torque logging. Mirror a smaller grid in sim for under one A100-day to choose the cells. Rough cost: mostly robot time, under $1k GPU.",
      "compute_after": "If relative transformation restores retention, parallel pose-randomized sweeps can rank features by generalization half-life across tasks and models. More compute then buys a map of which internal directions are portable skills and which are absolute-coordinate memories.",
      "exact": "Primary estimand is R(d, theta) with paired CI. Call a direction portable only if R >= 0.8 at 20 cm and 45 deg after transformation while untransformed R <= 0.5 at the same point. Also report measured pose-estimation error and how much of the success drop is explained by adding that noise to the transform.",
      "expected": "Untransformed steering should decay quickly with displacement if it encodes absolute motor programs. Object-relative transformation should help only when the VLA has a usable pose representation; expected recovery is partial for insertion and poor for cloth if cloth state or pose is uncertain.",
      "fails_if": "The object-relative transform does not raise R above about 0.5 at 10 cm/15 deg, or the residual failure is fully explained by pose-estimation error around 1 cm/2 deg or more; then more steering compute is not the blocker and hardware/state estimation should be fixed first.",
      "closest_prior": "Grant et al. motor programs bound to absolute coordinates, 50/50 grasps at the recorded UR10e spot; pi0.5 SAE steering on DROID, +9 to +21 out of 25 target-object grasps; COAST pi0.5 gains on LIBERO and real tasks."
    }
  ]
}
